Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Microsoft 365 OAuth device code authentication flow (Kali365 token theft) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Attacker device registration in victim Entra tenant after device-code compromise · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Microsoft 365 sign-in from Kali365 phishing infrastructure IPs · [LLM] Endpoint connection or DNS lookup to Kali365 Cookie Link AitM domains · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Kali365 post-compromise mailbox hiding rule (spam/phish/click/link/SharePoint keywords) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Microsoft 365 OAuth device code authentication flow (Kali365 token theft) Exploitation Medium
Hunts successful Entra/M365 sign-ins completed via the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant, the core technique Kali365 abuses to steal session tokens and bypass MFA. Device code flow is rare in most tenants, so a sudden appearance — especially for new users or unusual client apps — is a strong account-takeover signal. Rationale: Built on Kali365's defining TTP — abuse of Microsoft's OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant (microsoft.com/devicelogin) to mint tokens without solving MFA. Arctic Wolf and the FBI PSA both center the campaign on device code flow; reprise99's Sentinel repo confirms the AuthenticationProtocol=='deviceCode' detection pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://github.com/reprise99/Sentinel-Queries/blob/main/Azure%20Active%20Directory/Identity-DeviceCodePhishing.kql • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/05/22/fbi-warns-of-kali365-as-device-code-phishing-soars/5245024
ATT&CKT1566 T1528 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
// Device code flow marker lives in AuthenticationProcessingDetails when the dedicated AuthenticationProtocol column is unavailable
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| extend ProcDetails = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
| where ProcDetails has "Device Code"
| summarize SignInCount = count(), Apps = make_set(Application), SrcIPs = make_set(IPAddress), Countries = make_set(Country), arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AccountUpn
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Application, IPAddress, Country, City, DeviceTrustType, SignInCount, Apps, SrcIPs, Countries
| order by Timestamp desc
// Canonical field is AuthenticationProtocol == "deviceCode"; this tenant schema exposes AuthenticationProcessingDetails, parsed below
let Lookback = 14d;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ResultType == 0
| extend ProcDetails = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
| where ProcDetails has "Device Code"
| summarize SignInCount = count(), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName), SrcIPs = make_set(IPAddress), Locations = make_set(Location), arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by UserPrincipalName
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IPAddress, Location, ClientAppUsed, SignInCount, Apps, SrcIPs, Locations
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft 365 OAuth Device Code Authentication Flow

description: Detects successful Entra/M365 sign-ins completed via the OAuth device authorization grant, abused by Kali365 for MFA-bypass token theft.
references:

logsource:
  product: azure

detection:

  condition: selection
level: medium
CLOUD
index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" "properties.authenticationProtocol"="deviceCode" "properties.status.errorCode"=0
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values("properties.appDisplayName") as apps values(src_ip) as src_ips dc(src_ip) as ip_count by user

[LLM] Kali365 post-compromise mailbox hiding rule (spam/phish/click/link/SharePoint keywords) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts creation of malicious Outlook/Exchange inbox rules that auto-move and mark-as-read messages matching Kali365's documented keyword set (spam, phish, click, link, SharePoint). Arctic Wolf observed operators planting these rules immediately after device-code token theft to suppress security warnings and victim replies. Rationale: Uses Arctic Wolf's exact reported rule logic — keyword set (spam/phish/click/link/SharePoint) combined with move-to-folder + mark-as-read actions designed to hide phishing-warning and reply traffic. The keyword+action pairing makes this far more specific than a generic 'new inbox rule' alert. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-phishing-kali365-microsoft365-access-tokens/
ATT&CKT1564.008 T1114.001
Data sources
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in~ ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","Update-InboxRules","UpdateInboxRules")
| extend Raw = tolower(tostring(RawEventData))
| where Raw has_any ("spam","phish","click","link","sharepoint")
| where Raw has_any ("movetofolder","markasread","deletemessage","junkemail")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, ActionType, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Operation in~ ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules")
| extend params = tolower(tostring(Parameters))
| where params has_any ("spam","phish","click","link","sharepoint")
| where params has_any ("movetofolder","markasread","deletemessage","junk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, OfficeWorkload, Parameters
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
index=o365 sourcetype="o365:management:activity" Operation IN ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules")
| eval params=lower(_raw)
| where like(params,"%spam%") OR like(params,"%phish%") OR like(params,"%click%") OR like(params,"%link%") OR like(params,"%sharepoint%")
| where like(params,"%movetofolder%") OR like(params,"%markasread%") OR like(params,"%deletemessage%") OR like(params,"%junk%")
| table _time, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, Parameters
| sort - _time
[LLM] Attacker device registration in victim Entra tenant after device-code compromise Installation Medium
Hunts Entra ID 'Add registered device' / device-join audit events that Kali365 operators used to register attacker-controlled devices into compromised tenants, extending persistent access beyond the stolen token. High-value when correlated to a recent device-code sign-in or an anomalous source IP. Rationale: Targets Arctic Wolf's reported post-access step of registering new devices into the victim's Microsoft environment to extend access. Device-registration audit operations are the canonical telemetry for T1098.005 and are corroborated across the campaign write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://therecord.media/fbi-warns-of-kali365-phishing-attacks
ATT&CKT1098.005 T1078.004
Data sources
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "Entra" or Application has "Azure Active Directory"
| where ActionType has_any ("Add registered device","Register device","Add device","Add registered owner to device")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, ActivityObjects, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OperationName has_any ("Add registered device","Register device","Add device")
| where Result == "success"
| extend Initiator = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InitiatorIP = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.ipAddress)
| extend TargetDevice = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Initiator, InitiatorIP, TargetDevice, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Entra ID Device Registration Following Device-Code Compromise (Kali365)

[LLM] Endpoint connection or DNS lookup to Kali365 Cookie Link AitM domains Command & Control High
Detects corporate endpoints resolving or connecting to Kali365-controlled domains (kali365.xyz, v2/api subdomains, duemineral.uk) used for the affiliate panel and the 'Cookie Link' adversary-in-the-middle mode that proxies victims to capture session cookies and tokens. Any internal host touching these domains indicates phishing interaction or attacker tooling. Rationale: Direct IOC match on the pre-extracted Kali365 domains (kali365.xyz and subdomains, duemineral.uk) tied to the affiliate panel and Cookie Link AitM proxy. An internal endpoint touching these is unambiguous phishing/C2 interaction; wildcard *.kali365.xyz catches new subdomains. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://hackread.com/fbi-kali365-phishing-service-microsoft-365-account/

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8") or SHA1 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8") or MD5 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8") or SHA1 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8") or MD5 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
